butir.teks: Explanation of what has been altered in the terms of the sciences
Know that the source of the confusion of the blameworthy sciences with the religious sciences is the distortion of the praiseworthy names, their alteration, and their being transferred by purposes

that are corrupt to meanings other than what the righteous early generations (salaf) and the first generation intended. They are five terms: jurisprudence (fiqh), knowledge, affirmation of Divine oneness (tawhid), admonition, and wisdom. These are praiseworthy names, and those described by them are the holders of positions in the religion, but they have now been transferred to blameworthy meanings, so hearts have come to recoil from censuring anyone who is characterized by their meanings, because these names are so commonly applied to them.

The first term is fiqh. They have acted upon it by restriction, not by transfer and conversion, in that they restricted it to knowing the unusual subsidiary cases in legal opinions, standing on the subtleties of their reasons, speaking much about them, and memorizing the statements related to them. Whoever is deeper in delving into them and more occupied with them is said to be the most learned in fiqh. Yet in the first era the name fiqh applied unrestrictedly to knowledge of the path of the Hereafter, knowledge of the subtleties of the afflictions of the selves and of what corrupts deeds, a strong grasp of the pettiness of this world, intense yearning for the bliss of the Hereafter, and fear taking hold of the heart. What shows you this is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ⟦QS 9:122⟧ And what brings about the warning and the frightening is this fiqh, not the ramifications of divorce, manumission, li'an, salam, and hire. For these do not bring about any warning or frightening; rather, devoting oneself to them continually hardens the heart and removes fear from it, as we see now in those who devote themselves to them.

Allah Most High says, ⟦QS 7:179⟧ and by it He meant the meanings of faith, not legal opinions. And by my life, fiqh and understanding are, in the language, two names for one meaning; it is only that the discussion concerns the customary usage of it, anciently and in modern times.

Allah Most High says, ⟦QS 59:13⟧ the verse. So He ascribed their little fear of Allah and their magnifying the might of creatures to their scant fiqh. So consider whether that is the result of not memorizing the ramifications of legal opinions, or the result of lacking the sciences we have mentioned.

And he said (peace and blessings be upon him) to those who came to him as a delegation, "Scholars, jurists."(١) And Sa'd ibn Ibrahim az-Zuhri (may Allah have mercy on him) was asked, "Which of the people of Medina is the most learned in fiqh?" He said, "The most God-conscious of them toward Allah Most High." It is as if he pointed to the fruit of fiqh, and God-consciousness (taqwa) is the fruit of inner knowledge, not of legal opinions and judgments.

And he said (peace and blessings be upon him), "Shall I not inform you of the faqih, the complete faqih?" They said, "Yes." He said, "The one who does not make people despair of the mercy of Allah, does not make them feel secure from the plotting of Allah, does not make them lose hope in the relief of Allah, and does not abandon the Qur'an out of aversion to it for something other than it."(٢) And when Anas ibn Malik narrated his saying (peace and blessings be upon him), "For me to sit with a people remembering Allah Most High from morning until the rising of the sun is dearer to me than to free four slaves,"(٣) he said: he turned to Zayd ar-Raqashi and Ziyad an-Numayri and said, "The gatherings of remembrance were not like these gatherings of yours, where one of you delivers his exhortation to his companions and recounts hadith at length. Rather, we would sit and mention faith, ponder the Qur'an, gain understanding in the religion, and count the blessings of Allah upon us, as an act of understanding." So pondering the Qur'an and counting blessings were called understanding (tafaqquh).

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "A servant does not fully understand until he loathes people for the sake of Allah and until he sees the Qur'an as having many aspects."(٤) It is also reported as a saying halting at Abu ad-Darda (may Allah be pleased with him), together with his words, "Then he turns to himself and is yet more severe in loathing it." And Farqad as-Sabakhi asked al-Hasan about a matter, and he answered him. He said, "The jurists differ with you." Al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "May your mother lose you, Farqad! Have you seen a faqih with your own eye? The faqih is only the renunciant (zahid) in this world, desirous of the Hereafter, insightful in his religion, constant in the worship of his Lord, scrupulous (wara'), restraining himself from the honor of Muslims, abstinent from their wealth, sincere in advice to their community." And in none of that did he say, "the one who memorizes the ramifications of legal opinions." I do not say that the name fiqh did not include legal opinions on the outward rulings, but it was by way of
generality and inclusion, or by way of consequence, so their applying it to the knowledge of the Hereafter was more frequent.

From this restriction there emerged a deception that drove people to devote themselves to it and to turn away from the knowledge of the Hereafter and the rulings of the hearts. And they found in their nature something that helped them in this, for inner knowledge is obscure, acting upon it is hard, and using it to seek office, judgeship, status, and wealth is unattainable. So Satan found room to make that appear fair in hearts by means of restricting the name fiqh, which is a praiseworthy name in the Sharia.

The second term is knowledge. This used to be applied to knowledge of Allah Most High, of His signs, and of His acts among His servants and His creation, so much so that when 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) died, Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "Nine-tenths of knowledge has died," for he made it definite with the article and then explained it as knowledge of Allah, glorified and exalted is He. And they have also acted upon it by restriction, so that they made it, for the most part, famous for the one who busies himself with disputation with opponents in juristic questions and others. So it is said, "He is the scholar in truth, the champion in knowledge," while one who does not practice that or busy himself with it is counted among the weak, and they do not count him in the company of the people of knowledge.

This too is an act of restriction, but most of what has been reported of the merits of knowledge and of scholars concerns those who know Allah Most High, and His rulings, His acts, and His attributes.

And now it has come to be applied unrestrictedly to one who encompasses nothing of the religious sciences except dialectical outlines on disputed questions, so he is counted by that among the champions of the scholars, despite his ignorance of exegesis (tafsir), reports, the knowledge of the school, and the like. And this has become a destructive cause for many of the seekers of knowledge.

The third term is tawhid. It has now been made an expression for the craft of theology (kalam), knowing the way of disputation, mastering the ways of refuting opponents, and the ability to hold forth in it by multiplying questions, raising doubts, and composing compelling arguments, to the point that groups of them styled themselves "the people of justice and tawhid," and the theologians (mutakallimun) called the scholars "scholars of tawhid," although nothing of what characterizes this craft was known at all in the first era; rather, strong censure came from them against anyone who opened a door of disputation and wrangling. As for what the Qur'an contains of clear proofs that minds race to accept at the first hearing, that was known to all, and knowledge of the Qur'an was knowledge in its entirety. And tawhid, in their view, was an expression for something else that most theologians do not understand, and if they understand it they are not characterized by it: it is that one sees all matters as from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, a seeing that cuts off one's turning to causes and intermediaries, so that one sees all good and evil only as from Him, exalted is His majesty. This is a noble station, one of whose fruits is reliance on Allah (tawakkul), as its explanation will come in the Book of Reliance.
And among its fruits also are giving up complaining about creatures, giving up anger at them, and contentment (rida) and submission to the ruling of Allah Most High.

And one of its fruits was the saying of Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) when it was said to him during his illness, "Shall we seek a physician for you?" He said, "The Physician made me ill." And the saying of another, when he fell ill and it was said to him, "What did the physician say to you about your illness?" He said, "He said to me: I am the Doer of whatever I will."
And evidences for that will come in the Book of Reliance and the Book of Tawhid.

And tawhid is a precious jewel, and it has two husks, one of which is farther from the kernel than the other. People have restricted the name to the husk and to the craft of guarding the husk, and have neglected the kernel altogether. The first husk is that you say with your tongue, "There is no god but Allah." This is called tawhid, in contrast to the Trinity that the Christians declare openly, but it may come from the hypocrite whose inner contradicts his outer.

And the second husk is that there be in the heart no contradiction or denial of the meaning of this saying; rather, the outward side of the heart comprises belief in it and likewise assent to it. This is the tawhid of the common people, and the theologians, as has preceded, are the guardians of this husk against the disturbance of the innovators.

And the third, which is the kernel, is that one sees all matters as from Allah Most High, a seeing that cuts off one's turning to intermediaries, and that one worships Him with a worship by which one singles Him out, so that one worships none other. Following caprice (hawa) falls outside this tawhid, for everyone who follows his caprice has taken his caprice as his object of worship.
Allah Most High said, ⟦QS 45:23⟧ And he said (peace and blessings be upon him), "The most hateful god worshipped on the earth
Rather, the place of the gaze of Allah Most High, which is what is interpreted, is the heart, which is the mine of tawhid and its wellspring.

The fourth term is remembrance (dhikr) and admonition. Allah Most High said, ⟦QS 51:55⟧ And many reports have come in praise of gatherings of remembrance, such as his saying (peace and blessings be upon him), "When you pass by the gardens of Paradise, graze." It was said, "What are the gardens of Paradise?" He said, "The gatherings of remembrance."(٢) And in the hadith: "Allah Most High has roaming angels in the world, besides the angels of creation. When they see gatherings of remembrance, they call to one another: Come to what you seek! So they come to them and surround them and listen. Beware, so remember Allah and remind yourselves."(٣) Then that was transferred to what you see most preachers of this time persisting in, namely stories, poetry, ecstatic utterances (shath), and extravagant claims (tammat). As for stories, they are an innovation (bid'a), and a prohibition from the early generations against sitting with storytellers has been reported. They said, "That was not in the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him)(٤) nor in the time of Abu Bakr nor 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) until the trial arose and the storytellers appeared." And it is reported that Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) came out of the mosque and said, "Nothing brought me out but the storyteller; had it not been for him, I would not have gone out."
